messages:
aj: Heads-up — ACME (AE flagged) is asking for 99.99% monthly uptime in us-west-2 + a hard p95 <= 50ms for generation endpoints, and a Premium support tier with 15-min P1 response. They say it's a renewal condition.

maria: OK. can you paste the exact ask/contract language? need specifics: measurement windows, what counts as downtime, and any exclusions.

aj: AE copy: 'Customer requires 99.99% monthly availability for api.redwood.com scoped to us-west-2, 95th percentile end-to-end latency <= 50ms for generation endpoints measured at ingress for successful requests, and 24/7 hotline with 15-min P1 response. Failure to meet SLAs subjects vendor to service credits.'

neal: Engineering reality check: 50ms p95 for hosted generation is not achievable for the larger models we serve. Current p95 is ~120–200ms for our smaller quantized models and 500–800ms for the big-decoder family. 50ms is only plausible with dedicated capacity + smaller model variants or aggressive model pruning.

sam: SRE notes: to sign off on an uptime/latency SLA we need clear SLIs, error budget accounting, and automated SLO reporting per-customer. Also need on-call escalation + routing to ensure priority requests land on SLA pools. We should define 'availability' at the frontend gateway and exclude scheduled maintenance plus upstream network failures.

tara: Support perspective: 15-min P1 response requires a dedicated priority queue, rotas, and documented runbooks. We also need an SLA mapping in Zendesk and a way to flag customer tickets as 'SLA: Premium' so they skip normal SLAs. That is non-trivial ops work.

maria: Proposed product options to present to AE/customer:
  A) Redwood Dedicated offering: 99.99% + 50ms p95 with monthly GPU reservation (12-mo recommended), full priority routing, and premium support.
  B) Hosted SLA (availability + credits) + Premium support (15-min response) but no latency guarantee — cheaper & faster.
  C) Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) with custom SLAs.
We need cost delta and lead times for each.

oliver: Legal: we need precise definitions in contract: where availability is measured, latency percentile calculation, success criteria for requests, maintenance windows, force majeure, and cap on service credits. Draft sample clause below — product to confirm tech constraints.

oliver: ```
Availability: "Availability" means the percentage of 1-second ingress checks for which the Service responds with a 2xx status code, measured monthly, excluding Scheduled Maintenance and Customer Network Failures.
Latency: "Latency" means the 95th percentile of end-to-end request duration for successful generation requests measured at the gateway.
Remedy: Service credits up to 5% of monthly fees per violation; cumulative cap 20%.
```

neal: Tech work required if customer chooses A or requires latency guarantee on hosted: per-customer low-latency routing, priority scheduling/admission control, KV cache pinning or prewarm hooks, and runtime telemetry to export per-customer p95. Also gating by model size (deny huge model runs on low-latency pool).

sam: Rough schedule estimate: infra/routing + admission control = 6–8w; runtime cache pinning + prewarm = 3–4w; telemetry & per-customer SLO dashboards = 2–3w; ops/runbooks = 1–2w. Ballpark 12–14 weeks to support full latency SLA on hosted.

maria: That timeline is significant. We need a go/no-go from GTM: is this prioritized over the queued roadmap items (batching optimizer, rollout UI, cost-monitoring)? If not, suggest offering option B or C.

aj: Customer expects an answer this week. AE asks for a list of options + required commitments and lead times. Can we give them staged options (fast availability SLA today, latency-guarantee later with commit)?

maria: Action items:
- Neal: tech impact doc + constraints and gating (due Mon).
- Sam: proposed SLIs/SLOs, error budget rules, and draft escalation/playbook (due Tue).
- Oliver: contract template with explicit exclusions and credit caps (due Wed).
- Tara: support staffing impact + cost estimate for premium support (due Wed).
I'll bundle and present options to AE on Thu.

aj: I'll tell AE we can provide options and rough timeline; will try to buy one week.

sla-bot: New intake created: SLA-INTAKE-1796000123. Assigned: product/maria; labels: enterprise, uptime, latency, premium-support.

maria: Note for pricing: for a 50ms p95 guarantee on gen we'll likely require dedicated pool + 12mo commit; price band accordingly.

neal: One more technical detail: define 'successful requests' — must exclude streaming cancellations and client-side timeouts to avoid skewing latency numbers. I'll add exact definitions in the tech doc.

tara: :thumbsup:

(threads: short, we'll keep updates in this thread; if/when AE confirms I'll create a cross-functional ticket and link here.)
